rejected.rule: Mode names (block, inline, note) stay unprefixed: the prefix avoids clashes with stylesheets that import ours, and none does.
The global parameters celex and converter are the stylesheet's public interface, set by name from Java.
Stylesheets are documented in comments, not Oxygen's xd:doc.
Each module is checked on its own, so a function another module calls looks unused.
The rule doesn't read prefixes used in XPath (map:, fn:, lt:), so it reports used declarations.
// is used where a construct can occur at any depth (notes, included documents, quotations); keys index the hot lookups.
for-each is used over computed sequences (annex groups, lines, markers), where there is no node to match.
Push style: one small template per Formex element is the design.
name() and local-name() are used for error messages and Formex element names, deliberately.
f:legal-text is the document's outline: one template that lays out the parts in order.
